answer: The glacier multiplier is published, charged in nadir, and beacon lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3139 identities would post 3415 proofs and burn roughly 61 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
